entities.summary: Johannes van Keulen (active 1660-1715) was a prominent Dutch cartographer who made lasting contributions to the field of nautical navigation. His most influential works include the comprehensive nautical atlas, the Zee-Atlas, and the pilot guide, the Zee-Fakkel. These publications not only showcased his expertise but also set a new standard for cartography in the Netherlands. By providing detailed and accurate maps of the world's oceans, van Keulen's works facilitated safe passage for merchant ships and naval vessels, thereby playing a crucial role in the growth of global trade.
